title: Bigger models, bigger valuations, and Washington's mixed signals
body:
This month the index tilted toward a few powerful owners holding very capable AI. Enslaved God, the 'genie in a box' ending, stayed on top and rose from 36.0 to 38.5. Benevolent Dictator (+2.8), Protector God (+2.4), Zookeeper (+2.2) and Descendants (+2.1) also gained, while Libertarian Utopia (-0.7), Self-Destruction (-0.3), Egalitarian Utopia (-0.2) and Reversion (-0.1) slipped. Horizon Balance ended at 2.5, a little above the 2.1 it started at, after dipping to 0.7 on 21 May and climbing to 3.0 on 4 June.

Capability drove much of it. Google I/O launched always-on agents, an OpenAI model disproved an Erdos conjecture checked by outside mathematicians, and Anthropic shipped Opus 4.8 and then Claude Fable 5. Money concentrated at the same time: the jury rejected Musk's case against OpenAI, Anthropic raised at about $900B and then filed for an IPO at $965B post-money, and SpaceX, owner of xAI, listed at about $1.75T.

Washington swung back and forth. Trump scrapped an AI testing order on 21 May, signed a scaled-back version on 2 June, and a bipartisan draft bill on 4 June would require frontier safety frameworks. Then on 12 June an emergency export-control directive forced Anthropic to shut down Fable 5 worldwide, sinking Gatekeeper by 1.1 in a day.

Across the month, Capability Velocity rose 1.6, Power Concentration 2.4, AI Autonomy 1.6, and Alignment & Control 1.2, while Global Coordination fell 0.8.
